newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdynia shipyard to end 1996 in red.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdynia shipyard to end 1996 in red.

text.p: The Polish Gdynia shipyard is likely to end this year with a net loss of several million zlotys but should return to the black in 1997, its president Krzysztof Banaszak told a news conference on Tuesday.

"After the first three quarters of the year the shipyard's revenues were 650 million zlotys and should be 945 million at the end of the year, but the company will have a negative net result of several million," Banaszak said.
"The losses stem from contracts, not always good, struck with a French shipowner for bulk carriers in 1993 and 1994. But we expect a small net profit next year" he added.
He said the shipyard faced a restructuring programme, envisaging modernisation and laying off some 500 workers, for which it needed a government-guaranteed loan.

"The shipyard has asked for a government-guaranteed loan of $60 million for that purpose from a banking consortium led by the Polish Development Bank (PBR)," Banaszak said, adding however, it was unclear when the guarantee would be granted.
The Gdynia shipyard has contracts for construction of 36 ships worth a total $1.3 billion, which fills its sales plan until 1999. It is negotiating a further 32 contracts worth some $1.4 billion.

The shipyard is owned 47 percent by the state treasury, while PBR manages 40 percent of the shares belonging to the biggest commercial Bank Handlowy SA and the commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA. Small shareholders have a 13 percent stake in Gdynia.
